ledger.claim: The rider is not a repeat claimant and the heightened corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08 does not bite. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the threshold of 4 that clause sets, and it is the only rider-profile field POL-RD-08 permits anyone to rely on for this test. There is no basis on this record for treating the claim as one that needs more than the ordinary evidence.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and says in terms that trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy that may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The trace records 21.20 km against a booked optimal of 18.40 km: an excess of 2.80 km, or 15.2% of optimal. The percentage limb of the establishment test requires the excess to exceed 20% of optimal; 20% of 18.40 km is 3.68 km and the excess is 2.80 km, so the limb fails. Both tests must pass, and POL-RD-01 provides that if either fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The trace is impaired at weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE; the point survives that discount because POL-RD-07(i) directs the excess across the impaired stretch to be measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes, which is the reading most favourable to the driver and is the reading I rely on.

The trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: there is a single 428.0 s gap between consecutive fixes, more than four times the 90 s limb (a), running from the Defu Flyover portal fix to the Kallang portal fix. Under POL-RD-07(i) the excess across that stretch is the straight line between the bounding fixes, expressly because that is the reading most favourable to the driver. Measured that way the trip is 21.20 km and sits below the POL-RD-01 threshold. The 25.50 km surface-route figure that would cross the threshold is a reconstruction, not a measurement, and no artifact in this bundle carries it. The trace is impaired at weight 0.39 (GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE).

There is no driver admission in the chat log: the driver's only message says he is going by the KPE, which is the corridor the platform's own optimal route uses - optimal_route_source reads 'optimal is KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries'. erp_gantries is null, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-00110 at weight_multiplier 0.39 but does not name its issue code(s): GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE

ledger.claim: The surviving chat shows the driver volunteering the corridor he was taking - 'going KPE ah boss' at 18:25:50 - and the rider answering 'ok' 24 seconds later, and the platform's own optimal route for this trip is the KPE then the ECP. The rider had notice of, and did not object to, the very corridor the platform routed him along, so the route driven is not an off-corridor route he can complain of. I do not put this forward as a POL-RD-04 rider-requested detour: no rider message identifies a place or road, and both waypoint_hint fields are null, so that clause is unavailable on this record and I do not rely on it. The chat log is impaired at weight 0.6 with issue TRUNCATED_LOG.

On the fare, no line is unmatched. The rider's own claim concedes $3.00 of ERP; the fare breakdown charges tolls_erp of 3.00, which equals trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd of 3.00 for a route the platform describes as crossing both gantries on the optimal corridor. Gantry-by-gantry matching is not possible because erp_gantries is null, and POL-RD-09(4) directs that where no coordinates are carried the match is undecidable, the line is treated as matched, and the ruling must say so. There is accordingly no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). The fare breakdown is impaired at weight 0.75 with issue PARTIAL_RECORD.

The rider's complaint is really about the 39 minute duration. POL-RD-01's establishment test is a distance test - excess over the optimal distance measured on the trace. Elapsed time enters this policy only as optimal_duration_min inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation has already been established. No deviation is established here, so the metered time charge stands and the duration gives the rider no separate ground of complaint.

POL-RD-06's profile check is engaged only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, which requires excess above 50% of optimal or above 8.0 km. The excess here is 2.80 km and 15.2%, so the materiality gate is not reached, no pattern test is required and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is licensed. For completeness on the test the clause does name, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 744 completed_trips_90d over the same window: there is no repeat-deviation pattern and no conduct referral is open. Nor is this a case where POL-RD-06(a) could matter, because the case is not genuinely balanced - the excess fails the threshold on the reading most favourable to the driver.

There is no driver admission in the chat log: the driver's only message says he is going by the KPE, which is the corridor the platform's own optimal route uses - optimal_route_source reads 'optimal is KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries'. erp_gantries is null, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The counterparty statement asserts the same KPE route and admits nothing. And trip_record.actual_distance_km is, on the pre-pass's own assessment, derived from this very trace, so it is not independent corroboration. The chat log is itself impaired at weight 0.6 with issue TRUNCATED_LOG (last message 18:26:14, 2,186 s before the trip ended); I do not assert what was said after that point. Without an independent source the claimed refund cannot be ordered.
discarded_claims.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-FARE-00110 at weight_multiplier 0.75 but does not name its issue code(s): PARTIAL_RECORD

discarded_claims.claim: The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). The trace is impaired - a 428.0 s gap and coverage of 81.7% - and no source in POL-RD-07(ii)'s list exists on this record. The second limb of the rider's burden is therefore not discharged and the driver is never put to an exculpatory clause at all.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case cannot be decided on the present record, so it goes to a human reviewer. No money moves — the disputed S$10.00 is held rather than collected or refunded, and the S$34.42 charge stands until that review. The trigger is POL-RD-10(3), read with POL-RD-07(iii).

The only GPS trace, EV-GPS-00110, is impaired for policy purposes (not merely for schema): a single 428.0-second gap between consecutive fixes, 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, more than four times the 90-second limb of POL-RD-07(a), plus coverage of 81.7% (LOW_COVERAGE). The gap runs between the Defu Flyover portal fix and the Kallang portal fix, a 6.90 km straight line, and covers the whole stretch the rider disputes.

Because the trace is impaired, POL-RD-07(i) requires the excess across the gap to be measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes — the reading most favourable to the driver — which puts the trip at 21.20 km against a booked optimal of 18.40 km: 2.80 km, or 15.2%, just under POL-RD-01's 20% gate. But a surface route between the same two portals would put the trip at 25.50 km and over that gate, and nothing in the bundle distinguishes the two. This is therefore not a case where the trace ran and found nothing: the one stretch that decides the case is the stretch the trace cannot measure. POL-RD-07(iii) directs ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION on exactly this footing — absence of proof on a broken trace is a data failure, not a finding for the driver. I have considered the driver's submission that the driver-favourable measurement falls below the POL-RD-01 gate and that the outcome should be NO_ACTION. Even on that reading the case does not close: the figure that would decide it is carried only by the impaired trace (weight 0.39), because the trip record and the fare ledger are copies of the same measurement and not independent carriers, so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence cannot exceed 0.39 — below the 0.70 floor — which independently requires escalation under POL-RD-10(1) as well.

No independent corroboration of the POL-RD-07(ii) kind exists, and I have named each candidate and said why it fails:
• Chat log EV-CHAT-00110 is impaired (weight 0.60; issue TRUNCATED_LOG — the export stops at 18:26:14, 2,186 seconds before the trip ended). Its only driver message, 'going KPE ah boss', describes the corridor the platform's own optimal route uses ('optimal is KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries'), not a deviation, and nothing said later is in evidence. The rider's 'ok' shows notice, not consent to a detour.
• Fare breakdown EV-FARE-00110 is impaired (weight 0.75; issue PARTIAL_RECORD — erp_gantries is null against tolls_erp of 3.00), so the gantry-corridor test cannot be run at all. Applying POL-RD-09(4), an un-itemised gantry line with no coordinates is treated as matched and undecidable; accordingly there is no billing-integrity correction and no phantom charge, since trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is also 3.00.
• Trip record EV-TRIP-00110 (weight 1.00) and the fare ledger both carry 21.20 km, but both are copies of this trace, so neither is an independent source.
• The driver's counterparty statement ('I took the KPE like always') asserts the optimal corridor and admits nothing.
The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00110-01, is absent (weight 0.0; MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 closure exoneration has nothing behind it, and the driver's 'my phone loses signal in the tunnel' is not an exculpatory clause that can stand over the charge. POL-RD-04 is not available on this record: no rider message identifies a place or road and both waypoint_hint fields are null, so the corroboration test cannot be run. POL-RD-05 is not engaged (no amended endpoints and amended_optimal_distance_km is null).

On the remaining points: POL-RD-06 is not engaged — the excess (15.2% and 2.80 km) is far short of the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 744 completed_trips_90d — so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. POL-RD-08's heightened corroboration requirement does not bite (rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below 4), but it does not assist the rider either, because the trace is impaired. The 39-minute duration gives no separate ground of complaint: POL-RD-01 is a distance test, and time enters this policy only through the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which never runs.

What would resolve this case for the reviewer: the un-truncated in-app chat for the trip; gantry-by-gantry ERP itemisation (or gantry coordinates) placing the vehicle on or off the optimal corridor; an independent measurement of the gap stretch not derived from this trace; or an LTA traffic advisory covering the KPE/ECP in the 18:19–19:02 window.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
